name: as_factor
title: Convert labelled values to a factor

origin.description: Replaces labelled values with their labels and returns a factor.
origin.usage: as_factor(x, levels = c("default", "labels", "values", "both"), ordered = FALSE, only_labelled = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A labelled vector or a data frame.

arguments.name: levels
arguments.text: How to build the levels: "default", "labels", "values", or "both". A unique prefix is enough.

arguments.name: ordered
arguments.text: When true, the factor is ordered.

arguments.name: only_labelled
arguments.text: On a data frame, leave columns that are not labelled alone.

origin.details: The default uses a label where one exists and otherwise the value, sorted by the value. "both" prefixes the label with the value. "labels" turns unlabelled values into missing. "values" uses the codes.
origin.value: A factor. On a data frame, the labelled columns are replaced.

translation.description: Replaces labelled values with their labels and returns a factor vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A labelled vector or a data frame.

arguments.name: levels
arguments.text: How to build the levels: "default", "labels", "values", or "both". A unique prefix is enough.

arguments.name: ordered
arguments.text: When true, the factor is ordered.

arguments.name: only_labelled
arguments.text: On a data frame, leave columns that are not labelled alone.

translation.details: The default uses a label where one exists and otherwise the value, sorted by the value. "both" prefixes the label with the value. "labels" turns unlabelled values into missing. "values" uses the codes.
translation.value: A factor. On a data frame, the labelled columns are replaced.
translation.example:
from haven import as_factor, labelled
x = labelled([1, 2, 1, 2, 10, 9], {"Unknown": 9, "Refused": 10})
print(as_factor(x).values)
print(as_factor(x).levels)
